correctness.rationale: The theorem is correct. In any part, the closed-neighborhood sum equals the number of vertices outside the part minus twice the number of negative labels outside it, plus the label of the tested vertex. The standard minimality witness for a positive vertex then forces at least floor((N-L)/2) negative vertices, whether its tight witness is positive or negative. Placing exactly that many negatives outside a largest part satisfies every closed-neighborhood inequality, and every positive vertex sees a tight witness in the largest part, so the function is minimal. Fresh independent brute force over every unordered multipartite profile through total order eight and every sign labeling matched the formula.
